chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿUmar ibn Udhaynah, who said:
I wrote to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام asking him about a narration of al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī which he narrates from ʿAlī عليه السلام.
"Regarding the eye of a four-legged animal, if it is gouged out, then one quarter of its price is due."
So he said: "Al-Ḥasan has spoken the truth; ʿAlī عليه السلام indeed said that."

key_terms.رُبُعُ ثَمَنِهَا: one quarter of its price or market value
key_terms.رِوَايَةِ: a transmitted report or hadith being asked about
key_terms.صَدَقَ: he spoke truthfully; his report is affirmed
key_terms.عَيْنِ: the eye, the injured organ under discussion
key_terms.ٱلْحَسَنِ ٱلْبَصْرِيِّ: al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī, the narrator cited in this report

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on compensation for gouging out the eye of a four-legged animal in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning injury done to an animal. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام confirms the report from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام that the compensation for gouging out the eye of a four-legged animal is one quarter of its value. It reflects the jurisprudential concern for financial liability in cases of harm to property and animals.
